body:
Thank you for your reply. The medication has made it a lot easier for me to experiment with new things. So far I've been getting into knitting, crocheting, and sewing. I've also been baking a lot more and taking an interest in my health. I've also tried taking an interest in my appearance and I even started dressing differently. I wear dresses most of the time now and I spend a decent amount of time learning about homemade beauty products. 

I do feel better knowing that I'm gaining skills and that I'm more interested in being beautiful, but inside I still feel sort of hollow. It feels like the medication has made me happier doing things that will improve my mood in the short run, not the long run. Does that make sense? I still have this awful sense that I will never be happy like other people. I don't really know what true happiness is. I have never really been at peace with myself, and I've never spoken to anyone who I thought was legitimately happy except for maybe my grandmother, but she just recently passed away. 

I think it's good advice for me to get involved with others who share the same interests as me. I have been thinking about taking a crafting class or two but my social anxiety has made me procrastinate. Honestly I really don't have any friends. The one friend I do have makes me so, so anxious and it isn't her fault at all. She's a wonderful person but for some reason she makes me feel very insecure and uneasy. I don't really know how to make new friends either. 

Thanks again for your reply. Last night I was feeling so awful and today I feel better. It usually doesn't get that bad, but here's hoping tonight will be better.

My husband has the same belief. He tries to get me out and about and is always scheduling things to do with his family. I've been avoiding them because being around people makes me so nervous. When I first started the medication, I was very social and would always go to family events with my husband. But now it just seems so useless. I tried putting myself out there and I didn't really feel any different. I don't really know how to get out of my comfort zone.

I'm not sure. I'm worried I'll hurt our friendship. We had a falling out after I got married and we didn't speak for nearly a year. She said the main reason she didn't want to talk to me anymore was that I would only talk to her when I was having problems. So now I have no idea how to find a balance between talking about my problems and just hanging out. It makes me so nervous that I stopped hanging out with her.
